tagline: Dragon's Back, Lion Rock and the four great trails: Hong Kong's green secret.
why: Most visitors don't realise that about 40% of Hong Kong is country park. Hiking is one of the city's favourite weekend activities, with dramatic peaks, beaches and trails minutes from skyscrapers. Hikers talk about routes, difficulty, views and the weather. Knowing the famous trails and some hiking lingo makes you great company and might get you invited along.

essentials.title: Country parks
essentials.body: Hong Kong has 25 country parks covering about 40% of its land, with well-marked trails and distance posts.

essentials.title: The four long-distance trails
essentials.body: MacLehose Trail (100 km, New Territories), Wilson Trail (78 km), Hong Kong Trail (50 km, Hong Kong Island) and Lantau Trail (70 km). Each is split into stages.

essentials.title: Famous hikes
essentials.body: Dragon's Back, Lion Rock, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak, Sharp Peak, Tai Mo Shan (the highest peak at 957 m), Ma On Shan and the Twins.

essentials.title: Beaches and islands
essentials.body: Hikes often end at beaches: Tai Long Wan in Sai Kung, Big Wave Bay, Cheung Sha. Islands like Lamma and Cheung Chau make easy day trips.

essentials.title: Weather and safety
essentials.body: Heat, humidity and typhoons are serious. Check warnings, carry plenty of water, and avoid hiking in heavy rain or very hot weather.

essentials.title: Hiking culture
essentials.body: Weekend hiking with friends, colleagues and hiking groups; many people end with seafood or a beer.

names.name: Dragon's Back
names.what: Hong Kong Island ridge walk once named Asia's best urban hike, ending at Big Wave Bay.

names.name: Lion Rock
names.what: Iconic rock that symbolises the 'Lion Rock Spirit' of perseverance.

names.name: Lantau Peak
names.what: The second-highest peak; sunrise hikes are popular.

names.name: Sunset Peak
names.what: Lantau peak famous for silvergrass in autumn.

names.name: Sharp Peak
names.what: A challenging, pointed peak in Sai Kung with stunning beach views.

names.name: Tai Long Wan
names.what: Hong Kong's most beautiful beaches, in Sai Kung East.

names.name: MacLehose Trail

now.headline: Hiking boom continues
now.detail: Covid made hiking hugely popular, and many newcomers kept going.

now.headline: Trail running races
now.detail: Events like the Hong Kong 100 ultra attract international runners.

now.headline: Rescue calls
now.detail: More hikers means more rescues, especially in heat; safety campaigns are common.

now.headline: Country park debates
now.detail: Housing proposals near country park edges spark arguments.

local.headline: Weekend ritual
local.detail: Saturday or Sunday hikes followed by food are a classic social plan.

local.headline: Easy starters
local.detail: Dragon's Back, Lamma Island and Violet Hill are good beginner hikes.

local.headline: Getting there
local.detail: MTR, minibus, taxi and ferries reach most trailheads.

local.headline: Best seasons
local.detail: October to March is ideal; summer is hot and humid.

debates.question: Best hike in Hong Kong?
debates.sides: Dragon's Back for ease, Sharp Peak for drama, Lantau Peak for sunrise.
